title: Why Is It So Hard to Make a Good Weather App? - The Atlantic
summary: Charlie Warzel explores the world of weather forecasting and the reliability of weather apps on smartphones. He discusses the public's obsession with these apps, their frequent complaints about inaccura racy forecasts, and the importance of understanding and conveying the inherent uncertainty in weather predictions. Adam Grossman, co-creator of the popular Dark Sky app, explains the complex process of making weather predictions, including the use of satellites, balloons, simulations, and machine learning. Despite advancements, the chaotic nature of weather makes accurate forecasting challenging.
sentiment_reason: The article discusses the public's reliance on weather apps and their dissatisfaction with the accuracy of these forecasts, highlighting the negative sentiment around the topic.
